action_criteria.expected_evidence: WBC 13.6 x10^9/L with CRP 52 mg/L; potassium 3.2 mEq/L and magnesium 1.5 mg/dL; sodium 130 mEq/L; creatinine 1.3 mg/dL; bilirubin 7.8 mg/dL, albumin 2.2 g/dL, INR 2.4, platelets 78 x10^9/L; ammonia 142 µmol/L supportive only
action_criteria.label: Core laboratory work-up: blood count, electrolytes, renal and liver function, glucose, INR, ammonia and CRP, with toxicology where alcohol or drugs are in question
action_criteria.rationale: Confirms liver dysfunction and identifies metabolic and infective precipitants [ACG_HE_2026]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Blood cultures: no growth at 48 hours
action_criteria.label: Blood cultures, two sets, before the first antimicrobial dose
action_criteria.rationale: Fever 38.2 °C with leucocytosis: blood cultures are drawn before the first antibiotic dose [EASL_HE_2022]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Ascitic PMN 124 cells/mm3, below the 250 cells/mm3 threshold for SBP
action_criteria.label: Diagnostic paracentesis: cell count with differential, total protein and albumin, Gram stain and culture in blood-culture bottles
action_criteria.rationale: Every hospitalised patient with cirrhosis, ascites and encephalopathy needs a diagnostic paracentesis to exclude SBP, here with fever and leucocytosis as well

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No pyuria; urine culture no growth at 48 hours
action_criteria.label: Urinalysis and urine culture before the first antimicrobial dose
action_criteria.rationale: Fever with leucocytosis: the urinary tract is screened alongside blood and ascites before antibiotics [EASL_HE_2022]

action_criteria.label: Chest radiograph: fever after a respiratory illness two weeks earlier
action_criteria.rationale: Fever 38.2 °C with WBC 13.6 after a respiratory illness two weeks earlier and no source on paracentesis, urinalysis and cultures: pneumonia must be excluded, since infection is the commonest precipitant of overt HE [EASL_HE_2022]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: C. difficile GDH antigen negative and toxin B gene PCR not detected
action_criteria.label: Stool Clostridioides difficile testing: five days of diarrhoea with fever in cirrhosis
action_criteria.rationale: Four to five loose stools a day for five days with fever and leucocytosis: C. difficile colitis must be excluded before the diarrhoea is attributed to lactulose [EASL_HE_2022]

action_criteria.label: Non-contrast CT head
action_criteria.rationale: No focal deficit, seizure or head trauma, so imaging is optional; it excludes hemorrhage or mass if the course is atypical or there is no response to treatment [ACG_HE_2026]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Generalized triphasic waves with diffuse delta slowing; no epileptiform discharges or seizures
action_criteria.label: EEG
action_criteria.rationale: Diffuse slowing supports a metabolic encephalopathy and excludes non-convulsive seizures [EASL_HE_2022]

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No relevant rifaximin or lactulose interaction; propranolol reduced or stopped if hypotension, sodium below 130 or kidney injury; spironolactone held; insulin dose reduced; avoid sedatives
action_criteria.label: Medication review: rifaximin and lactulose against propranolol, spironolactone and insulin glargine, and sedatives
action_criteria.rationale: No concrete interaction changes management; the review confirms beta-blocker, diuretic and insulin adjustments in acute illness [EASL_decomp_2018]

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give benzodiazepines or other sedatives for agitation or sleep: they precipitate and prolong hepatic encephalopathy; manage agitation with reorientation, a safe environment and treatment of the precipitant (EASL 2022).
Do not prescribe sedating opioids, which worsen hepatic encephalopathy; use acetaminophen up to 2 g per day for pain.
Do not escalate lactulose while he already has 4-5 loose stools per day with hypokalemia.
required_recommendations: Restart rifaximin 550 mg twice daily with lactulose to prevent recurrence (ACG 2026; EASL 2022), and secure the supply before discharge (prior-authorization appeal, patient-assistance program or social work) so that the insurance gap does not recur.

Reduce lactulose to the dose that gives 2-3 soft bowel movements per day (currently 4-5 loose stools per day with potassium 3.2 mEq/L); correct potassium and volume, and investigate persisting diarrhea rather than attributing it to lactulose.

Replace potassium to 4.0 mEq/L or more, because hypokalemia increases renal ammoniagenesis, and replace magnesium (1.5 mg/dL); hold spironolactone while overt HE, the diarrhea and the creatinine of 1.3 mg/dL persist (EASL 2018).

Fever 38.2 °C with leukocytosis and no source on paracentesis (PMN 124), urinalysis, chest radiograph and stool C. difficile testing: start empirical antibiotic cover after cultures, and narrow or stop it according to the cultures at 48 hours (EASL 2018).
Blood, urine and ascitic cultures are drawn before the first antibiotic dose, which is not delayed for them.
Give parenteral thiamine before any glucose (prior heavy alcohol use).
Refer for liver transplant assessment: decompensated cirrhosis with overt HE, MELD-Na 30 (EASL 2018); support continued abstinence.

avoided_actions.rationale: No clinical suspicion for hepatopulmonary syndrome, portopulmonary hypertension, or endocarditis; echocardiography is not part of the HE workup.
Amyloid PET has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the issue, not Alzheimer pathology.
DaTscan has no role in HE workup; the question is metabolic encephalopathy, not nigrostriatal degeneration.
Early-onset AD genetic panel has no role in HE workup; reversible metabolic encephalopathy is the diagnosis under consideration.

accepted: Hepatic encephalopathy (West Haven grade III), alcoholic cirrhosis (Child-Pugh C, MELD-Na 30), precipitated by rifaximin non-adherence x 10 days (insurance gap) plus diarrhea-associated hypokalemia; fever with leukocytosis requires exclusion of SBP and other infection.

differential.key_features: Fever and ascites make SBP the first infection to exclude; the ascitic PMN of 124 cells/mm3 (below 250) with a sterile culture excludes it.

differential.diagnosis: Other infection (pneumonia, Clostridioides difficile colitis, bacteremia)
differential.key_features: Fever 38.2 °C, WBC 13.6 and CRP 52 with no source after paracentesis and urinalysis; blood and urine cultures sterile, chest radiograph without consolidation after the respiratory illness, and stool negative for C. difficile despite five days of diarrhea. An occult infection is not excluded by early sterile cultures, so empirical cover continues until they are final.
Less suggested by tox; monitor regardless.
No focal deficit, fall or seizure; a CT, if obtained, shows no hemorrhage.

key_clinical_evidence: HE is a clinical diagnosis: West Haven grade, evidence of liver disease and exclusion of other causes of altered mental status (ACG 2026; EASL 2022).

Precipitant identification is more actionable than the ammonia number: infection (SBP especially), GI bleed, electrolyte disturbance (hypokalemia/hyponatremia), constipation, sedative/CNS-depressant use, dehydration, dietary protein load, renal failure.
Medication-access gaps (insurance, copays) are common, often missed precipitants — ask about pill supply directly.

Lactulose is the secondary prophylaxis after a first overt episode; rifaximin 550 mg twice daily is added to lactulose after a recurrence, and stopping it is a recognized precipitant (ACG 2026; EASL 2022).
Child-Pugh C (15: bilirubin 7.8 3, albumin 2.2 3, INR 2.4 3, moderate ascites 3, HE grade 3 3); MELD-Na 30 (creatinine 1.3, bilirubin 7.8, INR 2.4, sodium 130)

An elevated ammonia neither grades nor confirms hepatic encephalopathy and repeat levels are not used to guide treatment; a normal ammonia in a confused patient with cirrhosis should prompt a search for another cause (ACG 2026 recommendation 5 and key concept 14; EASL 2022).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Fever 38.2 °C with leucocytosis after a recent respiratory illness may be attributed to a viral infection; with ascites and HE, SBP must still be excluded by paracentesis. Here the PMN of 124 excludes it, and the fever then needs a chest radiograph and stool C. difficile testing.
red_herrings.data_point: Fever 38.2 °C with leukocytosis (WBC 13.6) after a respiratory illness two weeks earlier
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attribute the fever to a resolving viral respiratory infection and skip the diagnostic paracentesis.

metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate HE: alcoholic cirrhosis with a 10-day rifaximin gap from an insurance problem and diarrhea-associated hypokalemia as precipitants; fever with leukocytosis requires SBP and other infection to be excluded
metadata.difficulty_rationale: Required: core labs, blood and urine cultures and a diagnostic paracentesis; EEG recommended, CT and medication review optional.
